agreed_facts.text: Paul Mackenzie was sentenced to 200 years in prison.
The convictions cover the deaths of 190 children and one adult, 191 people in total.
Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve themselves or their children to death.
The starvation was ordered so that followers could meet Jesus.

headline_quotes.quote: Doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 190 children
Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years
an edict that was violently enforced, a court heard during his trial

emphasis.text: Leads with the doomsday character of the cult and the order to starve in order to meet Jesus.
The New York Times reports that the starvation edict was violently enforced, according to the trial.
The Daily Mirror describes the sentence as a life sentence.

headline_quotes.quote: his apocalyptic religious cult
starve their children to death in a forest
starved to death on his orders in Shakahola Forest

emphasis.text: Places the deaths in a forest, named by France 24 as Shakahola Forest.
BBC News describes the sentence as a life sentence for murdering 191 people.

omissions.text: Centre coverage does not mention that the starvation edict was violently enforced, as heard at trial.
Left coverage does not mention the forest setting of the deaths, including Shakahola Forest.

headline_quotes.quote: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence
Kenya cult leader Paul Mackenzie sentenced to 200 years

emphasis.text: Foregrounds the order to starve and, in several articles, the aim of meeting Jesus.
Describes the group as a doomsday or apocalyptic cult or sect.

headline_quotes.quote: Kenyan starvation cult leader sentenced to 200 years for child murders
A self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher

emphasis.text: Describes Mackenzie as a self-proclaimed preacher and the group as an infamous starvation cult.
States the sentence was handed down on Friday.

summary.text: A court in Kenya has sentenced cult leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult. He ordered his followers to starve themselves and their children to death, which some outlets say was so they could meet Jesus. France 24 places the deaths in Shakahola Forest.

stories.title: Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assaults; reactions and fallout

Brand faces further allegations of raping two more women, and more cases are expected.

‘I hope you are pleased with yourself’

emphasis.text: Leads with Brand's barrister, Ian Winter KC, reporting himself to a watchdog after a clash with Sunday Times journalist Rosamund Urwin.

He now faces "significant" prison time

emphasis.text: Reports the verdict by a London jury and the prospect of significant prison time.

headline_quotes.quote: There could be many more victims, says Met Chief

stark warning is made to other celebrities with a dark past

emphasis.text: Leads with the verdict and the prospect of further accusations and criminal charges.
Reports that Brand was remanded in custody ahead of sentencing on 9 November.

summary.text: A London jury found Russell Brand guilty of rape and three sexual assaults, and he was told he faces a significant custodial term, with sentencing on 9 November. He faces further rape accusations, and police expect more cases.

conclusion.text: All sides report Brand's conviction for rape and sexual assault and the prospect of further cases. Western outlets emphasise reactions and fallout, while Eastern outlets lead with the verdict and possible new charges. Accounts differ on whether a 16-year-old was among the convicted counts or the further accusations.
